title: Titanium Headset Spacer
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5, UNS R56400) was selected for this headset hardware application because its 900+ MPa tensile enables thin-wall lightweighting under cyclic loading. The alpha-beta microstructure provides 45% higher specific strength than 4140 steel, critical for weight-sensitive designs. Its 6.7 W/mK thermal conductivity simplifies thermal management. This rationale is driven by micro-adjusting headset spacer 1/3/5mm and service environment demands.
process: CNC turning Swiss-type for headset hardware geometry
Thread rolling DIN 13-1 6g with Class 6g gauge
Go/No-Go ring gauging with Class 6g gauge
surfaceTreatment: Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water
commonFailures: Bearing race brinelling from over-torque - avoided by torque-limiting press-fit tool with ±2% accuracy

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Headset Spacer suitable for Micro-adjusting headset spacer 1/3/5mm?
faq.a: Titanium Headset Spacer uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address headset hardware operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Headset Spacer?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Headset Spacer require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. headset hardware components receive Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the service environment.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Headset Spacer shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements; (4) Surface roughness certification on critical features. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Headset spacer / Steerer spacer headset hardware components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
